incidents.title: 11 Federal Agents Smash Into Apartment Building at 6 a.m. to Arrest Man for Anti-ICE Social Media Posts
incidents.summary: At approximately 6 a.m. on February 5, 2026, at least 11 Homeland Security Investigations officers in camouflage and masks broke through the security window of Eat Street Flats — a residential apartment building in Minneapolis's Whittier neighborhood — to arrest 37-year-old Kyle Wagner. Rather than contact the building's property manager or use the front door, agents smashed the glass beside the security entrance, then broke down Wagner's apartment door upstairs. Wagner was charged with cyberstalking and interstate communications out of the U.S. Attorney's Office in Eastern Michigan for allegedly doxxing a pro-ICE individual and making threatening social media posts against ICE agents. The broken security window left the building's entrance unsecured for all residents.
incidents.location: Eat Street Flats, Franklin Ave & Nicollet Ave

incidents.title: Kidney Transplant Recipient Arrested in Rochester Needs Anti-Rejection Medication
incidents.summary: Federal immigration agents arrested Javier Abreu, 38, on Civic Center Drive in Rochester on February 5 while he was delivering groceries for his church. Agents rammed his car and broke his window during the arrest. Abreu is a kidney transplant recipient who requires anti-rejection medication, and State Rep. Kim Hicks says his access to the medication has been inconsistent. He was transported to the Whipple Federal Building near Ft. Snelling and was scheduled to be flown to a facility in Texas on February 6.
incidents.latestUpdate: Wife and attorney [confirm Abreu is finally receiving](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2026/02/09/kidney-transplant-recipient-in-ice-custody-is-finally-getting-meds-wife-and-attorney-say) his anti-rejection medications.
incidents.location: Civic Center Drive and Broadway Avenue

incidents.title: Jose Lozano Detained Despite Valid Asylum Permit in Worthington
incidents.summary: Jose Lozano, 28, was detained by ICE while jumpstarting his minivan outside his Worthington home despite holding a valid asylum permit with three years of authorization remaining. When he attempted to retrieve his wallet to show documentation, agents prevented him from doing so. An immigration attorney intervened within 30 minutes to stop his transfer to Texas.
incidents.latestUpdate: Lozano [released at approximately 11:00 PM](https://www.dglobe.com/news/local/worthington-man-back-home-after-five-days-in-ice-custody) after five days in ICE custody. Volunteers transported him back to Worthington; he arrived home around 2:00 AM on Feb 4. Plans to return to work at JBS and classes at Minnesota West Community & Technical College. Hearing date set for February 28.

incidents.title: Citizen Check: ICE Agents Surround U.S. Citizen Family Home in Rochester
incidents.summary: ICE agents surrounded the home of the Fareh family in Rochester on Sunday, February 1, 2026, while Abdirashid Fareh's siblings were home alone, including a 12-year-old sister with special needs. The family are U.S. citizens born in Rochester. No arrests were made, but the 12-year-old refused to go to school the following day. Fareh testified about the incident at the Rochester City Council meeting on February 2.

incidents.title: U.S. Citizen Detained at Olmsted County Government Center, Released After Identity Verified
incidents.summary: ICE agents followed a U.S. citizen of Latino heritage to the Olmsted County Government Center in Rochester on January 31, 2026, and detained him amid outcry from observers and local legislators. The man was released after his identity was verified. Rochester Police Chief Jim Franklin said DHS officials described the detainment as a traffic stop, which he said ICE is allowed to make if agents suspect a driver is undocumented.

incidents.title: NATIFS Restaurant Employee Detained at Gunpoint, Flown to Texas
incidents.summary: An employee at NATIFS (North American Traditional Indigenous Food Systems), the nonprofit Indigenous food organization run by James Beard Award-winning chef Sean Sherman, was pulled from a vehicle at gunpoint by federal agents outside the Minneapolis restaurant and flown to Texas by morning. Sherman told Mother Jones that agents blocked in a car carrying several staff members, drew their guns, and said they were "just going to check his paperwork" before transporting him to Texas. The employee is from Ecuador and reportedly had legal documentation. Sherman stated his employees "are not criminals" and "don't have police records."

incidents.title: Columbia Heights High School Students Harassed by ICE Agents
incidents.summary: Three Columbia Heights High School students had their cars surrounded by ICE vehicles while lawfully driving to school on the morning of January 29. One 16-year-old student was forced to show their passport to masked federal agents. Another student called the school principal in fear, leaving a voicemail saying agents were "looming around the high school." Superintendent Zena Stenvik reported ICE agents were parked behind the high school in a park and circling schools that morning.

incidents.title: Second St. Paul Public Works Employee with Legal Work Status Detained
incidents.summary: A second St. Paul Public Works employee was detained by ICE during the week of January 29, 2026. Public Works Director Sean Kershaw stated the worker "had full legal right to work" and was detained "based purely on their country of origin." The employee is now being held in El Paso, Texas and is connected with a lawyer.

incidents.title: U.S. Citizen Luis Martinez Subjected to Facial Recognition Scan
incidents.summary: Luis Martinez, a U.S. citizen, was boxed in by federal agents in a Minneapolis suburb while driving to work. Masked agents demanded his ID, then held a phone inches from his face and scanned his features using the Mobile Fortify facial recognition app. He was only released after producing his U.S. passport.

incidents.title: U.S. Citizen Detained Outside Rochester Bowling Alley, Released After Rep. Kim Hicks Intervenes
incidents.summary: A U.S. citizen was detained by ICE agents outside Bowlocity bowling alley in Rochester on January 23, 2026. The man was handcuffed and loaded into a vehicle before being released shortly after. When state Rep. Kim Hicks asked agents why they were arresting him, an agent responded that the "vehicle is going back to an illegal" — but Hicks confirmed the car was registered to the man himself.

incidents.title: CBP Detains Two Teenagers (One Confirmed U.S. Citizen) After Rear-Ending Their Vehicle, Deploys Tear Gas on Bystanders
incidents.summary: U.S. Customs and Border Protection officers handcuffed and detained two teenagers in south Minneapolis on Wednesday afternoon after allegedly rear-ending their silver SUV. The teenage girl driver, who presented a U.S. passport to agents, was still placed in handcuffs and was seen crying in the back of a federal vehicle. At least two bystanders were arrested and agents deployed tear gas and pepper spray as crowds gathered to film and protest the arrest.

incidents.title: Venezuelan Refugee Detained at Whipple Check-In, Flown to Texas with 60 Minnesota Women; Green Card Approved While in Custody
incidents.summary: A Venezuelan woman who entered the United States legally as a refugee was detained at a routine Whipple Federal Building check-in on January 21 and flown to El Paso, where she was held with approximately 60 other Minnesota women. Her green card application was approved while in detention, and she was released after Judge Tunheim's Temporary Restraining Order halting Operation PARRIS arrests on January 28.

incidents.title: Metro Police Chiefs Call for End to Civil Rights Violations / Racially Discriminatory Citizen Checks; Off-Duty Brooklyn Park Police Officer Stopped at Gunpoint, Asked for Papers
incidents.summary: Three Twin Cities law enforcement leaders held a joint press conference at the Minnesota State Capitol on January 20 to address a pattern of ICE agents conducting racially discriminatory citizenship checks on people of color. Brooklyn Park Police Chief Mark Bruley disclosed that an off-duty Brooklyn Park police officer—a woman of color and U.S. citizen—was stopped by ICE agents who boxed in her vehicle, drew their weapons, and demanded paperwork to prove her citizenship. When she attempted to record the encounter, agents knocked the phone from her hands. "If it's happening to our officers, it pains me to think of how many community members fall victim daily," Bruley said. Hennepin County Sheriff Dawanna Witt called the incidents "concrete examples of profiling," while St. Paul Police Chief Axel Henry said "people are scared to death, afraid to go outside—not because their status is in question but because they know people get stopped based on appearance."

incidents.title: U.S. Citizen Arrested Twice by ICE in St. Cloud After Mistaken Identity
incidents.summary: Mohamed Abdirizak Jama, a 36-year-old U.S. citizen who has held citizenship for 15 years, was arrested by ICE agents in St. Cloud on January 20 after they mistook him for another person. Court records confirm the mistaken identity. Frightened by unmarked vehicles chasing him, Jama tried to drive away before agents boxed him in. He was taken to the Whipple Federal Building at Fort Snelling and released. Approximately eight days later, he was arrested again on charges of interfering with a federal officer stemming from the first encounter.
incidents.location: Washington Memorial Drive and Division Street

incidents.title: ICE Agents Staying at Hotel Arrest One of Its Employees
incidents.summary: A Nicaraguan refugee working at the Hilton Homewood Suites in St. Louis Park was arrested by ICE agents who were staying at the hotel as guests. The man had a valid work permit through 2029 and entered the U.S. legally as a refugee in October 2023. Despite agents being informed of his legal status, they detained him as part of Operation PARRIS. A federal judge ordered his immediate release on January 25, 2026, noting the "Orwellian situation" created by bureaucratic delays.

incidents.title: Hmong U.S. Citizen Detained Shirtless in Freezing Weather, Then Released
incidents.summary: A Hmong man named Saly, described as a naturalized U.S. citizen with no criminal record, was reportedly detained by ICE agents who broke down his apartment door. According to family members, agents did not allow him to put on proper clothing before taking him outside in approximately 10-degree weather. After driving him around for nearly an hour, questioning, and fingerprinting him, agents released him after determining he had no criminal history. The family believes ICE was searching for someone who previously lived at the address.
incidents.latestUpdate: [KSTP investigation](https://kstp.com/kstp-news/top-news/man-ice-sought-in-humiliating-arrest-of-us-citizen-has-been-in-prison-since-2024/) reveals one of ICE's targets (Lue Moua) has been in state prison since September 2024; the other (Kongmeng Vang) got a driver's license at a Circle Pines address, not the Thao residence

incidents.title: U.S. Citizen College Student Restrained by ICE, Released After Showing Birth Certificate
incidents.summary: Perla Ocampo, an 18-year-old college student born in Willmar, Minnesota, was pulled from her vehicle by ICE agents, slammed against the car door, and restrained. She was released only after agents saw her birth certificate. In the days before this incident, ICE agents had followed her home from work on multiple occasions.

incidents.title: MSU Mankato Student Mohammed Hoque Detained by ICE a Second Time
incidents.summary: Mohammed Hoque, a 20-year-old Bangladeshi student at Minnesota State University, Mankato, was detained by ICE for a second time in mid-January 2026 during Operation Metro Surge. He was released on January 15 after several hours in custody. Hoque had previously been detained for 40 days in 2025 over pro-Palestinian social media posts, prompting a federal lawsuit. A federal judge found credible evidence of viewpoint-based targeting and ordered his release in May 2025.

incidents.title: Federal Agents Execute Search Warrant at Wrong Address; U.S. Citizen Mistakenly Arrested
incidents.summary: FBI, ATF, and Hennepin County Sheriff's Office agents used a battering ram to enter Alisa Porter's South Minneapolis apartment, handcuffing her daughter and searching the home. The warrant was for a different address—the man they sought had lived in the unit above Porter's but moved out two months prior. The search was connected to items stolen from FBI vehicles during protests over recent ICE shootings.

incidents.title: ICE Rams Into Parked Car, Demands U.S. Citizen Couple Show Citizenship Papers
incidents.summary: In January 2026, ICE agents rammed into a parked car belonging to Minneapolis resident Nadine and her Latino U.S. citizen husband, then cornered them with three vehicles. Despite being citizens, agents demanded the husband provide proof of citizenship. When Nadine attempted to exit her vehicle to photograph the ICE vehicle's license plate for insurance purposes, agents threatened her with obstruction charges. Agents refused to provide names or badge numbers. Nadine later filed a police report and learned the ICE vehicle's plates could not be located in police systems.

incidents.title: U.S. Citizen Detained Because of "Accent"
incidents.summary: Ramon Menera, a U.S. citizen, was detained by Border Patrol agents outside his home in a Minneapolis suburb in front of his 5-year-old daughter. The agent accused him of not being a U.S. citizen "because of your accent." Menera was eventually released but described the traumatic impact on his daughter, who asked him afterward: "Are you okay? They were going to take you? I don't want to lose you."

incidents.title: U.S. Citizen Born in Minnesota Detained by ICE for Two Days
incidents.summary: Nasra Mohamed Ahmed, a 23-year-old U.S. citizen born in Hennepin County, was detained by ICE agents on January 14 in the parking lot of her St. Paul apartment complex while on her way to pick up seizure and anxiety medication. Despite telling agents she was born in Minnesota and has never been to Somalia, she was held at Sherburne County Jail without bail for more than two days before being released to her family on Friday night (January 17) without charges. During detention, she suffered a stress-induced seizure and was taken to the hospital in full restraints. She later described being chained "like Hannibal Lecter" with a padlock. She has no criminal history.
incidents.latestUpdate: Nasra Ahmed describes being chained "like Hannibal Lecter" during hospital transport after suffering a seizure in detention.

incidents.title: ICE Agent Shoots Man Through Closed Door in North Minneapolis; Bullet Enters Apartment with Four Children
incidents.summary: On January 14, 2026, an ICE agent shot Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis, 24, in the leg during an arrest operation in north Minneapolis that began with a case of mistaken identity. DHS claims Sosa-Celis and two others attacked the agent with shovels. His partner, Indriany Mendoza Camacho, who was present and witnessed the events, disputes this — she says Sosa-Celis never grabbed anything and only tried to get inside the house. According to the defense, the agent fired through the closed front door after the men had gone inside. The bullet grazed Sosa-Celis' right thigh, then traveled through a wall into a first-floor apartment where four children and an adult were present, landing near a child's playpen. Both Sosa-Celis and co-defendant Alfredo Aljorna had Temporary Protected Status and were seeking U Visas. Agents later shot a tear gas canister through the apartment window. The two women present were detained, shackled at the feet, hands, and waist, and flown to a Texas detention center.
incidents.latestUpdate: ICE Director Todd Lyons [announces a joint criminal perjury probe with DOJ](https://www.npr.org/2026/02/13/nx-s1-5713947/immigration-agents-lie-minnesota) into two ICE officers who made "untruthful statements" under oath about the shooting. Both officers [placed on administrative leave](https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/news/todd-lyons-ice-north-minneapolis-shooting-lying-under-oath/) and face potential termination and criminal prosecution.

incidents.title: Three Oglala Sioux U.S. Citizens Still Detained at Fort Snelling (REMOVED)
Teen Refugee Handcuffed Driving to School, Held Overnight in Hotel Room with Federal Agents
incidents.summary: A high school junior living in St. Cloud was pulled over by ICE while driving to school on January 13. Despite showing her driver's license proving she is a minor, agents handcuffed her in the street and forced her to abandon her father's car. At the Whipple Federal Building, an agent told her to call her family — then threatened that if they came to pick her up, ICE would send the entire family to Texas. The teen spent the night in a hotel room with two federal agents before her attorney retrieved her the next day. At no point did anyone interview her about her refugee status or the reason for her arrest.
incidents.location: Traffic stop en route to school, then Whipple Federal Building, then unnamed hotel

incidents.title: Hmong U.S. Citizen Refuses to Open Door for Federal Agents
incidents.summary: Kong Vang, a U.S. citizen working from home in St. Paul's Frogtown neighborhood, recorded federal agents at his door and refused to let them in. The agents never explained why they were there and left after approximately 90 seconds. Vang's video went viral with over 400,000 views on Facebook.

incidents.title: U.S. Citizen Aliya Rahman Dragged From Car, Hospitalized After ICE Assault
incidents.summary: Aliya Rahman, a 43-year-old U.S. citizen and software engineer, was dragged from her car by ICE agents after they smashed her window. She was driving to an appointment at the Traumatic Brain Injury Center when agents blocked her path. After being taken into custody, Rahman repeatedly requested medical attention but was denied. She lost consciousness in her cell and was finally taken to a hospital, where she was treated for injuries consistent with assault. The video went viral with millions of views.
incidents.latestUpdate: Rahman [appears on Democracy Now](https://www.democracynow.org/2026/2/9/minneapolis_ice), describing ongoing trauma and how her autism and traumatic brain injury made it difficult to process auditory commands from agents during the assault. She also suffered a concussion at the Whipple Building.

incidents.title: U.S. Citizen Handcuffed at Willmar Convenience Store, Driven Away, Released in Parking Lot
incidents.summary: Alex Vasquez, a 34-year-old U.S. citizen from Willmar, was approached by ICE agents at a convenience store on 1st Street on a Monday afternoon. Agents requested identification, then handcuffed him and placed him in their vehicle. They drove him approximately one mile before releasing him in a fast food restaurant parking lot.

incidents.title: Citizen Check: U.S. Citizen Surrounded by ICE Agents at West St. Paul Restaurant
incidents.summary: Irma Escoto, a U.S. citizen born in New Mexico, was surrounded by ICE agents while sitting in her car outside El Taquito Taco Shop in West St. Paul. Her husband Luis Escoto, a naturalized citizen since 1992, rushed outside with her passport card to prove her citizenship. The couple co-owns the restaurant and believes she was targeted based on her appearance.
incidents.location: El Taquito Taco Shop, West St. Paul

incidents.title: U.S. Citizen Special Education Teacher Detained for Nearly 12 Hours
incidents.summary: Christina Rank, a 25-year-old special education paraprofessional and U.S. citizen, was detained by ICE for nearly 12 hours after an apparent vehicle collision with a federal agent's car in the parking lot of Concord Education Center, a school serving students with special needs.
incidents.location: Concord Education Center, Inver Grove Heights

incidents.title: ICE Rams Latino U.S. Citizen's Car, Releases Him After Confirming Identity
incidents.summary: ICE agents followed and rammed into the car of Christian Molina, a 40-year-old Latino U.S. citizen, two blocks from where Renee Nicole Good was killed. After demanding ID based on his appearance, agents released him when he proved citizenship. Molina described it as racial profiling.

incidents.title: Citizen Check: U.S. Citizen Confronted by ICE Agents While Walking
incidents.summary: Nimco Omar, a U.S. citizen and Somali American, was surrounded by four masked federal agents who demanded her identification during what they called a "citizen check" while she was walking near 24 Somali Mall in Minneapolis. Omar refused to show ID, asserting her constitutional rights. After repeatedly asking "Where were you born?" and photographing her without permission, the agents eventually walked away.

incidents.title: Green Card Holder Roughed Up by Agents, Held Over 10 Hours, Offered Money to Identify Immigrants
incidents.summary: Dennis Hernandez Ramirez, a 32-year-old Green Card holder who has lived in the U.S. for 25 years, was pulled over and "roughed up" by at least four federal agents while driving in Minneapolis. He was held for more than 10 hours at the Whipple Federal Building, where agents offered him money and legal protection in exchange for helping identify immigrants.

incidents.title: U.S. Citizen Detained by ICE in Brooklyn Park, Told to "Prove" Citizenship
incidents.summary: Rogelio Jimenez, a U.S. citizen, was forcibly removed from his car by masked ICE agents on Brooklyn Boulevard in Brooklyn Park. Despite repeatedly screaming that he was a citizen, an agent demanded he "prove it." He was handcuffed, placed in a federal vehicle, and driven around for approximately 20 minutes before being released. Agents claimed they were looking for someone with the same name.

incidents.title: Legal Permanent Resident Boxed In on Road, Handcuffed at Gunpoint; Agents Take Cash from Wallet
incidents.summary: Raul Aguirre Castrejon, a lawful permanent resident, was followed by two unmarked SUVs after leaving a Walmart in Monticello with his niece, a U.S. citizen. Agents boxed them in on the road, pulled Castrejon from the car at gunpoint, handcuffed him, and took $130 in cash from his wallet. Despite carrying proof of legal status, agents told him "you're not from here." He was released after a few minutes and later filed a sworn declaration in the ACLU's **Hussen v. Noem** lawsuit.

incidents.title: Multiple Airport Employees Detained by ICE at MSP
incidents.summary: Multiple airport employees were detained by ICE agents operating beyond security gates at MSP Airport. Union representatives report at least six employees with proper work authorization were "snatched" by agents, with four employees unreachable since detention.

incidents.title: Four Homeless Oglala Sioux Citizens Detained Near Little Earth (REMOVED)
incidents.latestUpdate: **REMOVED** — Tribe unable to confirm detained individuals are tribal members (see Correction Note above).
incidents.location: Under bridge near Little Earth Housing Project

incidents.title: Christian Refugee Detained, Shipped to Texas, and Dumped in Houston With No Way Home
incidents.summary: Thi Dua Vang, a Hmong refugee who fled Vietnam after decades of persecution for being Christian, was detained by ICE at her St. Paul home despite having legal status and a pending green card application. After nearly two weeks in detention—including being transferred to Texas and nearly deported before being pulled off a plane on the runway—an immigration judge ordered her release on bond. Since returning home, the family reports ICE agents have come back to their home three times.
incidents.latestUpdate: [MPR News reports](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2026/02/07/i-felt-hopeless-hmong-refugee-stranded-in-texas-after-release-from-ice-detention) Vang was forced outside after release from the Houston processing center. Agents refused to let her wait inside for her family: "They forced me outside and told me they didn't care if I lived or died." ICE had not returned her documents (Social Security card, state ID), preventing her from flying home.

incidents.title: Two U.S. Citizen Target Employees Detained and Injured
incidents.summary: Two Target drive-up employees, both U.S. citizens, were aggressively detained by CBP agents at the Richfield Target store. Both sustained injuries. According to witnesses, agents asked the workers if they were citizens; when they didn't answer and tried to go inside, they were grabbed and pinned to the ground. One affected individual, a 22-year-old Latino man identified in court documents as "Javier Doe," had a knee pressed into his neck, was driven around in an SUV while agents played loud music, and was eventually dumped in a Walmart parking lot in Bloomington. He required emergency medical care and is now a plaintiff in the ACLU class-action lawsuit against ICE.

incidents.title: Native American U.S. Citizen Punched and Detained by ICE
incidents.summary: Jose Roberto "Beto" Ramirez, 20, U.S. citizen and Red Lake Nation descendant, was punched and detained by ICE while driving to visit his aunt. Told he "wasn't from here." Released after family brought passport/birth certificate.
incidents.latestUpdate: Ramirez [voluntarily turned himself in](https://www.kaxe.org/minnesota-news/2026-01-28/red-lake-nation-descendant-charged-with-assaulting-ice-agent-during-detainment) after ICE returned to his home twice threatening arrest "the easy way or the hard way." He was charged under 18 USC 111 for allegedly assaulting an agent during his Jan 8 detention; released same afternoon.

incidents.title: U.S. Citizen Uber Driver Confronted by Agents: "I can hear you don't have the same accent"
incidents.summary: Ahmed Bin Hassan, 38, Somali American U.S. citizen and Uber driver, was confronted by over a dozen masked ICE/CBP agents at the airport. An agent stated: "I can hear you don't have the same accent as me." Hassan refused to show ID and challenged their authority.

incidents.title: U.S. Citizen Tackled by ICE at Shakopee Construction Site, Hospitalized
incidents.summary: Luis Ramirez Orozco, a Latino U.S. citizen, was tackled and detained by ICE agents at a construction site in Shakopee on the same morning Renee Good was shot by an ICE agent in Minneapolis. Despite identifying himself as a citizen, agents surrounded him and slammed his head on the floor. He suffered bruised ribs and a concussion, requiring medical attention.

incidents.title: Daycare Worker with Legal Status Detained While Running Errands, Sent to Texas
incidents.summary: Pablo Nieves, a staff member at Mis Amigos Spanish Immersion daycare in Golden Valley, was detained by ICE while running errands around January 7, 2026. According to the daycare's executive director, Nieves is in the country legally and has work authorization. He has been transferred to a detention facility in Texas. Another staffer's husband was also detained separately.

incidents.title: Naturalized U.S. Citizen Hospitalized After ICE Encounter
incidents.summary: Emmanuel Sackie, a Liberian-born naturalized U.S. citizen, was detained by ICE agents in a Family Dollar parking lot in Brooklyn Park. Despite showing his driver's license, agents demanded additional proof of citizenship. The encounter turned physical; Sackie was handcuffed, placed in a federal vehicle, and later hospitalized with significant bruising.

incidents.title: 20-Year U.S. Citizen Arrested Near Karmel Mall, Subjected to Racist Statements by ICE Agent
incidents.summary: Abdikadir Abdi Noor, a 43-year-old Fridley resident and trucking company owner who has been a U.S. citizen for approximately 20 years, was tackled and arrested by ICE agents on Pillsbury Avenue near Karmel Mall while trying to calm a crowd during a confrontation in which agents detained multiple people and kneeled on a woman's back for approximately 30 minutes. Noor had been asserting his constitutional rights and advising others of theirs. He was driven to the Whipple Building at approximately 85 mph without a seatbelt, shackled in a cell, and subjected to racist statements echoing Secretary Noem's rhetoric about Somali immigrants. He was released without charges at approximately 6:00 PM. Noor was subsequently arrested again in St. Cloud on January 12, 2026, and on January 29 was one of 16 people charged by the U.S. Attorney's Office with "violently assaulting federal officers and property."
incidents.latestUpdate: Corrected date from Dec 16 to Dec 15 per ACLU complaint. This incident occurred during the same confrontation as the [pregnant woman dragged through snow](/entry/2025-12-15-karmel-mall-pregnant-woman). Added ACLU complaint details, Noor's subsequent January 12 arrest in St. Cloud, and January 29 federal charges. Changed status to under-investigation.

incidents.title: Pregnant Somali Woman Dragged Through Snow at Karmel Mall
incidents.summary: ICE agents detained at least four people near Karmel Mall, the nation's first Somali shopping center. Witnesses reported a pregnant Somali woman was grabbed by the arms and dragged through the snow when she sat down to prevent falling. Agents were swarmed by 60-70 protesters, and one Somali U.S. citizen was released after detention.

incidents.title: U.S. Citizen Son of Rep. Ilhan Omar Stopped by ICE, Released After Showing Passport
incidents.summary: Adnan Hisri, the 20-year-old U.S.-born son of Rep. Ilhan Omar, was stopped by federal agents after leaving a Target store in Minneapolis. He was released after showing his passport. Rep. Omar said her son "always carries" his passport due to fears of racial profiling. DHS denied any record of the stop.

incidents.title: U.S. Citizen Questioned for Speaking Somali While Shoveling Snow with Mother
incidents.summary: Mahamed Eydarus, a 25-year-old U.S. citizen of Somali descent from Fridley, was detained by masked ICE agents on the morning of December 10, 2025, while shoveling snow with his mother after finishing an overnight shift as a personal care assistant. Agents surrounded him in unmarked vehicles, asked why he and his mother were speaking a "foreign language," demanded his mother remove her niqab (religious face covering), and separated him from his mother before eventually releasing them. Eydarus is now a plaintiff in the ACLU class-action lawsuit against ICE.

incidents.title: U.S. Citizen Tackled, Detained by ICE During Lunch Break
incidents.summary: Mubashir, a 20-year-old U.S. citizen and Somali American, was tackled, placed in a chokehold, and detained by ICE agents for several hours while on his lunch break in Minneapolis' Cedar-Riverside neighborhood. Despite repeatedly asserting his citizenship and offering to show his passport — with an agent responding "that don't matter" — agents refused to verify his status. He was transported to the Bishop Henry Whipple Federal Building, shackled, and initially told he would be deported. After his citizenship was confirmed hours later, agents refused to drive him back, forcing him to walk in the snow. In January 2026, Mubashir testified before Congress at a field hearing, telling lawmakers: "My citizenship did not protect me from being physically detained and hurt by ICE agents."
incidents.latestUpdate: [Testified at congressional field hearing](https://www.commondreams.org/news/minnesota-ice-abuse-testimony) in St. Paul hosted by Rep. Ilhan Omar and Rep. Pramila Jayapal, attended by nearly 30 U.S. lawmakers. Told Congress: "I repeated, 'I'm a citizen, I have an ID,' the agent kept saying, 'That don't matter.'" Said he was shackled at the federal facility and initially told he would be deported.

incidents.title: Somali Man with Temporary Protected Status Detained in Rochester
incidents.summary: A Somali man with Temporary Protected Status (TPS) valid until March 2026 was pulled from his car by ICE agents in southeast Rochester. The arrest was captured in a viral TikTok video and alarmed the local Somali community. Rochester Police confirmed ICE conducted an operation that day. A federal judge later ordered his release, finding he is not likely to be deported.
incidents.latestUpdate: [Federal judge ordered release](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2025/12/17/rochester-somali-man-ice-judge-orders-release), finding he is not likely to be deported to Somalia.
incidents.location: 14th Street SE near Meadow Park Apartments

incidents.title: Citizen Check: U.S. Citizen Detained 30 Minutes Outside Apartment Despite Showing Passport
incidents.summary: Ali Dahir, a 44-year-old Somali American U.S. citizen, was stopped by five ICE agents outside his Lake Street apartment building on December 2, 2025. Despite presenting his passport card and Minnesota driver's license, agents held him for 25-30 minutes in 19-degree weather before leaving when media and neighbors gathered.
incidents.location: Lake Street apartment building near Karmel Mall
